claimsToVerify: Patricians lived in spacious domus or villas while poor plebeians lived in crowded, multi-story wooden insulae.
Insulae in ancient Rome were notoriously prone to collapsing and catching fire.
The wealthy Roman workday typically ended around noon, after morning business and client meetings.
The typical poor Roman diet relied heavily on grain and bread, while the wealthy ate imported delicacies.
Both classes used public baths, though their experiences and social circles within them differed.
